prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Conroe, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1055; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was operating a sedan northbound on a city street in Conroe, Texas, and was executing a left turn at an intersection when the vehicle was struck on its driver side by a pickup truck, identified here as Driver 2's vehicle, which was proceeding straight through the intersection. Driver 1 stated that the impact jolted the body forward and then back against the seat, and reported pain in the neck and lower back. The force of the collision and the position of the vehicles are consistent with that type of injury. A passenger was seated in the front right seat of Driver 1's vehicle; both Driver 1 and the passenger were present at the scene and remained with the vehicle until assistance arrived. Photographs taken at the scene confirm the general point of impact and the resting positions of both vehicles. No independent witnesses to the collision were located. Several small scratches on the rear quarter panel of Driver 1's vehicle appear weathered and may predate this incident, and it could not be determined from the scene alone whether all of the body damage resulted from this impact. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the sedan.
